A solid trio could be Incineroar for Intimidate and disruption against Garchomp and Scizor, Kingambit to punish Gholdengo with Dark coverage, and Gholdengo itself if I can handle its Rotom-Wash matchup carefully since their Electric/Water typing is otherwise fairly neutral against it.

I'm weighing whether to use Parting Shot to pivot out while further weakening their attack, bringing in our own Garchomp, versus switching to Gholdengo whose Steel/Ghost typing and special attacks like Shadow Ball or Make It Rain hit neutrally but safely against their Garchomp.

Our Garchomp is faster at base 169 speed, so it can outpace theirs comfortably. The cleanest line is Parting Shot to tank their Garchomp's attack stat, then switch into our own Garchomp with Earthquake ready to punish it while it's weakened.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:

Gholdengo, being Steel/Ghost, would actually take double damage from Earthquake since Ghost doesn't resist Ground, so that's risky too. On the flip side, Gholdengo's Shadow Ball with Life Orb could do solid but non-lethal damage to the opposing Garchomp since it lacks a Ghost weakness, leaving switching in my own Garchomp with Rough Skin and Earthquake as the stronger option against theirs.

Their Garchomp is weakened at -2 attack, so its Earthquake against mine would hit much softer, especially since my Garchomp (Dragon/Ground) doesn't take extra damage from Ground-type moves. Mega evolving isn't instant, but just switching in gives me a speed and bulk advantage to threaten back with my own Earthquake.

Gholdengo would take super-effective damage from Earthquake and risks dying faster, while Garchomp resists that interaction better, so I'll switch into Garchomp.
